CEO Letter
An Open Letter from TRM CEO and Co-Founder Esteban Castano
Log in
Forensics

Overview
Capabilities
Put the power back in investigators’ hands.
Ardence is the AI investigation platform built for all-source intelligence. It brings connected intelligence and expert investigative methods into one reviewable investigation.
See how
Fight smarter with Ardence.
Ardence brings connected intelligence and expert investigative methods into one comprehensive inquiry. Under human direction, it uses AI to pursue more lines of investigation and follow relevant connections further.
Intelligence
Understand what no single source reveals.
Bring corporate, cyber, identity, dark web, financial, sanctions, and other intelligence into one investigation.
Speed
Search further. Move faster.
Pursue more lines of inquiry and follow connections further than a team can manage by hand.
Tradecraft
Put specialist methods to work.
Use expert-tested skills and repeatable analytic methods across teams, bringing specialized expertise into every investigation.
Disrupt
Turn findings into action.
Use reviewed evidence to draft legal process, submit asset freezes, or request infrastructure takedowns.
Criminal networks operate without limits.
No limits
Adversaries cross borders, change identities, and adopt new technology without any oversight. AI lets them multiply attacks, adapt tactics, and rebuild infrastructure faster than teams can investigate by hand.
Higher standards
Investigators face a different standard. They must separate a lead from a fact, account for where information came from, and stand behind every conclusion.
Limited resources
Fragmented intelligence, manual work, and scarce specialist expertise limit how far investigators can follow each lead.
Closing the gap
Investigators need to be able to find and disrupt criminal activity faster and more thoroughly without compromising evidence or human judgment.
Millions of data points, all working for you.
Ardence’s Data Network brings intelligence from TRM and specialized data providers into one investigation under a single Ardence contract.¹ Teams can follow connections across sources without negotiating separate provider contracts or assembling and maintaining the sources themselves.
¹ Provider availability varies by customer and jurisdiction. Supplemental terms may apply.
How to investigate with Ardence.
Start with the question.
Search across connected intelligence.
Apply expert methods.
Combine machine scale with human judgment.
The investigator defines the question, scope, and starting point: a person, organization, domain, IP address, email, account, wallet, or another known signal.
Ardence searches the intelligence sources available to the team and brings relevant records and connections into the same investigation.
Investigators use expert-tested skills and repeatable analytic methods to examine evidence, test connections, and pursue new leads.
Ardence keeps every finding connected to its sources, making the path from evidence to conclusion traceable and auditable. Investigators can review the evidence, understand what supports or challenges a finding, and own the conclusion.

CEO LETTER
An Open Letter from TRM CEO and Co-Founder Esteban Castano
Log in
Forensics
Request a Demo
Stop Illicit Crypto Transactions Before They’re Cashed Out
Join the industry's first real-time tracking and enforcement network
JOIN THE NETWORK
Read press release
What is Beacon Network?
Beacon Network is a real-time intelligence-sharing system that helps law enforcement, crypto exchanges, DeFi services, and stablecoin issuers stop illicit funds before they are withdrawn. Built by TRM Labs in collaboration with leading industry players, this crypto crime response network enables verified investigators to flag addresses linked to financial crime, immediately alerting exchanges and triggering risk-based responses.
A critical moment for crypto security
Crypto crime is evolving, and fragmented responses allow bad actors to exploit gaps. Recent hacks show how quickly stolen funds can move. Exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and law enforcement need a coordinated, real-time system to track and triage illicit assets before they disappear.
Flag
Verified investigators (exchanges, law enforcement, and security firms) flag illicit addresses in TRM
Trace
Flagged funds are auto-traced in real time as they move across the blockchain
Alert
When flagged funds reach an exchange or financial institution, Beacon Network immediately sends an alert
Action
Exchanges and issuers can review risk, work with law enforcement, and act before withdrawals occur
“Blockchain has proven to be one of the most powerful tools to fight financial crime, and Beacon Network further enables private and public sector collaboration to ensure that we continue to lower crime on the blockchain. We are looking forward to strengthening cross-collaboration through Beacon Network and proactively addressing risks and issues, allowing us to build more trust and security, which are the cornerstones of broader crypto adoption.”
Noah Perlman, Chief Compliance Officer, Binance
“There’s no program like Beacon Network. It’s a true early warning system that helps us identify and freeze illicit assets so law enforcement can recover them. That’s critical for protecting victims and safeguarding the broader ecosystem. Access to real-time intelligence is a game changer.”
Valerie-Leila Jaber, Global Head of Anti-Money Laundering, Coinbase
“When criminals move money, they do it fast — often using thousands of transactions across multiple wallets to obscure the trail. With the right real-time intelligence, we can follow the money and take action before it’s gone. That’s the shift Beacon enables: rapid detection and coordinated response, not hindsight.”
CJ Rinaldi, Chief Compliance Officer, Kraken
“As blockchain adoption accelerates across the mainstream financial system, maintaining trust and safety is essential to unlocking institutional adoption. Beacon Network represents a new chapter, defined by real-time intelligence, proactive risk management, and cross-sector collaboration. At Ripple, we’re proud to be a founding member.”
Andrew Rosenberg, Head of Financial Crimes Compliance, Ripple
“We’re proud to join the Beacon Network. This kind of public-private partnership is exactly what the industry needs to stay ahead of financial crime and represents a new standard for cooperation between crypto firms and law enforcement. At Zodia Custody, compliance and risk management are in our DNA, and we believe blockchain’s transparency is a powerful tool for smarter, faster financial crime prevention. Initiatives like the Beacon Network build on that potential and are critical to driving trust, accountability, and responsible growth across the digital asset ecosystem.”
Sophie Bowler, Chief Risk Officer, Zodia Custody

Compliance Center
TRM Labs is dedicated to earning and maintaining customer trust through world-class security and privacy practices. Our organization and infrastructure are certified to SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, and UK Cyber Essentials Plus standards.
Security and Compliance
TRM maintains a best-in-class security program and has completed and passed its SOC 2 Type II audit and will continue to build out its security infrastructure using the ISO 27001 framework, following GDPR principles. Our SOC 2 Type II audit report is available on request.
TRM data is stored in redundant, geographically dispersed data centers. Our data centers are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and managed under a TRM vendor management program.
In addition to our extensive internal scanning and testing program, TRM employs third-party security experts each year to perform a broad penetration test across the TRM Production and Corporate Networks. Executive summaries of test results are available upon request.
As part of the third-party vendor management process, management periodically reviews the performance of vendor entities by verifying that they maintain their relevant certifications (e.g., SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001:2013, PCI-DSS, etc.) by reviewing security and privacy control documentation captured in SOC 1 reports, SOC 2 reports, or other system and organizational documents, to validate the design and operating effectiveness of vendor controls.
For full details on our security program please
visit our Drata Trust Center.
ISO 27001
ISO 27001 is the leading global standard for information security, proving an organization has a robust, risk-based framework to protect sensitive data and maintain trust.
Request Download
ISO 27701
ISO 27701 is the international standard for privacy information management, extending ISO 27001 to demonstrate strong controls for protecting personal data and meeting global privacy regulations.
SOC 2 Type II
SOC 2 is a widely recognized audit standard that demonstrates strong controls for security, availability, and confidentiality, building trust with customers and partners.
UK Cyber Essentials Plus
Cyber Essentials Plus is a UK government-backed certification that independently verifies an organization’s cyber defenses, proving protection against common threats and reinforcing customer trust.
GDPR
GDPR is the European Union’s data protection regulation that enforces strict requirements for how personal data is collected, processed, and stored, ensuring privacy and strengthening individual rights.
System Status & Reliability
Our system status page gives you real-time updates on the availability and performance of our services.
See status
Modern Slavery Act Statement
The Modern Slavery act is legislation designed to combat forced labor, servitude, and human trafficking. Learn about TRM's policies and zero-tolerance approach to modern slavery and human trafficking.
Learn more
Privacy
At TRM, we take our customer's privacy seriously and are committed to protecting our customer's personal data. TRM complies with all applicable privacy laws and regulations. TRM processes personal data securely using appropriate technical and organizational measures, including our data governance practices, compliance standards, and risk management practices.
TRM is a member of the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework as set forth by the U.S. Department of Commerce.
View Privacy Policy
Social Impact
TRM is opposed to all forms of human trafficking, slavery, servitude, forced or compulsory labor, and all other trafficking-related activities. FAQ
What is TRM Deconflict?
A free deconfliction product from TRM that helps verified law enforcement officers coordinate on crypto-related investigations by checking if others are working the same wallet addresses and sharing context.
How much does TRM Deconflict cost?
TRM Deconflict is free for verified law enforcement users.
Who can use TRM Deconflict?
Verified law enforcement personnel from local, state, federal, and international agencies can use TRM Deconflict.
Does TRM Deconflict include training?
Yes. Users get access to selected TRM Academy resources to learn crypto basics and investigative best practices.
How do I sign up from TRM Deconflict?
Complete the
form below
with an official agency email and to request access and complete verification. TRM will confirm eligibility and enable your account.
How does TRM protect my data?
TRM applies strict security, access controls, and auditing appropriate for a law enforcement environment. Only verified users can access TRM Deconflict.
How does the platform notify investigators when overlapping wallets or subjects are detected?
When a submitted wallet overlaps with another active investigation, TRM sends alerts to the relevant verified investigators and a secure channel to request coordination without exposing case files.
What specific data do agencies share, and what information is never exposed?
Agencies share only essential identifiers such as wallet addresses and limited metadata for deconfliction. Full case narratives, suspect/victim PII, investigative tactics, and operational plans never leave the originating agency.

DPRK Crypto Threats: From Public Intelligence to On-Chain Tracing Session:
In this LEO Labs session, we will examine DPRK-linked crypto activity through a practical, case-based approach using publicly available and/or sanctioned information. The session will begin with a general intelligence overview of DPRK cyber-enabled revenue generation, including the role of cyber actors, IT workers, facilitators, and laundering networks. We will then use a public DPRK-linked case study, such as Sim Hyon Sop or Kim Sang Man, to demonstrate how investigators can move from open-source intelligence and sanctions reporting into on-chain tracing. The session will show how laundering layers can be identified, how exposure to services and potential off-ramp points can be developed, and how this type of analysis can generate investigative leads while remaining within safe and publicly shareable data.
